section_summary: This section chiefly documents applications, clearances, permits, and diplomatic correspondence concerning entry into Occupied Japan by commercial representatives, missionaries, diplomats, stateless travelers, and other foreign nationals. It also records revised SCAP procedures for routing applications through diplomatic missions or protecting powers, several China–Japan trade-related travel cases, and a dispute over customs and departure controls applied to Soviet personnel. Supporting materials include applications, biographical statements, action slips, telegrams, diplomatic notes, file forms, and correspondence acknowledging issued permits.

subfiles.title: Department of State letter forwarding Fred Kaunitz's passport information
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: Captain George H. Hendricks, Pacific Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Forwards Kaunitz's response concerning his Austrian passport and U.S. reentry permit.
subfiles.summary: The Department transmits Fred Kaunitz's requested travel-document information for consideration of his private-trader visit to Japan.

subfiles.title: Fred Kaunitz letter supplying travel-document details
subfiles.to: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Provides passport and U.S. reentry-permit numbers and validity dates.
subfiles.summary: Kaunitz supplies details of his Austrian passport and U.S. reentry permit in support of his application to visit Japan as a private trader.

subfiles.title: File charge sheet for Kaunitz papers
subfiles.about: Records the internal charging of papers from the file.
subfiles.summary: Blank or lightly completed records charge sheet accompanying the Kaunitz papers.

subfiles.title: William J. Melson application for permission to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests permission for Melson to develop import business and establish a Japanese office.
subfiles.summary: State Export Company applies for Polish national William J. Melson to visit Japan, contact business connections, and establish an office handling imports to the United States. The application identifies prewar radio-parts trade, intended visits to Yokohama and Tokyo, and an estimated three-month stay.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing William J. Melson's military permit
subfiles.from: Walter J. Marx for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Transmits Military Permit No. 4092 and explains the exit-permit waiver.
subfiles.summary: The Department sends Melson his military entry permit and advises that no U.S. exit permit is required.

subfiles.title: Telegram authorizing Nina Denisova Chirskoff and son to enter Japan
subfiles.about: Communicates Japan clearance for Chirskoff and her son subject to onward-travel documentation.
subfiles.summary: The Consul is instructed to certify clearance for Nina Chirskoff and her son George to enter Japan for sixty days, provided she holds valid travel and onward-admission documents.

subfiles.title: Action slip for Nina Denisova Chirskoff
subfiles.from: George H. Hendricks, Pacific Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Grants conditional clearance to Chirskoff and her son for a sixty-day stay.
subfiles.summary: Army clearance permits Nina Chirskoff and George to enter Japan, subject to consular approval and valid onward-travel documents.

subfiles.title: Action slip extending Mohamed Daneshvar's clearance
subfiles.from: George H. Hendricks, Pacific Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Extends Daneshvar's business-travel clearance through October 31, 1949.
subfiles.summary: Army authorities extend Mohamed Daneshvar's Japan entry deadline while retaining the original conditions.

subfiles.title: Diplomatic note concerning Mohamed Daneshvar's extension
subfiles.about: Confirms extension of Daneshvar's permission to enter Japan through October 31.
subfiles.summary: The Department informs the Iranian Embassy that military authorities approved the requested extension under the original clearance conditions.

subfiles.title: Foreign Missions Conference guarantee for Paul Gerhardt Möller
subfiles.from: Rowland M. Cross, Foreign Missions Conference of North America
subfiles.to: Walter J. Marx, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Guarantees logistical support for Möller's proposed six-week missionary visit.
subfiles.summary: Cross assures the Department that Möller will be supported in Japan and will undertake no commercial or unauthorized activities.

subfiles.title: International Missionary Council application for Paul Gerhardt Möller
subfiles.from: John W. Decker, International Missionary Council
subfiles.to: Walter J. Marx, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Requests permission for Möller to enter Japan for missionary conferences and consultations.
subfiles.summary: Decker describes Möller's travel document, itinerary, financial guarantees, and proposed consultations with Liebenzell missionaries and Japanese Christian leaders. Arrival was expected between October 15 and November 15, after a tour of Micronesia, for no more than six weeks.

subfiles.title: Abstract of the life history of Paul Gerhardt Möller
subfiles.about: Summarizes Möller's education, ministry, family, anti-Nazi record, and foreign travel.
subfiles.summary: The abstract presents Möller's theological education, church career, Gestapo hearings, nonparty status, marriage, and prewar and postwar travels.

subfiles.title: International Missionary Council letter of introduction for Möller
subfiles.from: John W. Decker, International Missionary Council
subfiles.about: Introduces Möller and requests assistance with permissions throughout his international missionary tour.
subfiles.summary: The Council guarantees Möller's reliability and funding while outlining prospective travel through Micronesia, Japan, China, Ceylon, Port Said, and Marseille.

subfiles.title: Department letter requesting a military permit for Möller
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: George H. Hendricks, Pacific Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Transmits the missionary application and requests a permit if theater clearance is granted.
subfiles.summary: The Department forwards Möller's application and support guarantee for military consideration.

subfiles.title: Army notification of Möller's theater clearance
subfiles.from: George H. Hendricks, Pacific Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Advises that Möller has theater clearance for two months as a special missionary visitor.
subfiles.summary: Hendricks directs Möller to apply through the State Department so a military permit can be issued.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing Möller's Military Permit No. 3089
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: John W. Decker, International Missionary Council
subfiles.about: Transmits Möller's permit for entry between October 15 and December 15.
subfiles.summary: The Department sends Permit No. 3089 and notes that Möller needs no U.S. exit permit.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 455 on Francisco José del Castillo y Campos
subfiles.about: Reports arrangements enabling the new Spanish mission chief to obtain passage to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy explains that it could not issue a Japanese visa but used a U.S. Army cable confirming del Castillo's clearance to prepare a facilitating letter. Del Castillo planned to join the SS Tegelberg at Buenos Aires after illness prevented boarding at Montevideo.

subfiles.title: U.S. Army cable confirming del Castillo's entry clearance
subfiles.about: Confirms entry clearance for the newly designated Spanish diplomatic mission chief.
subfiles.summary: SCAP asks that Francisco del Castillo be informed that his entry into Japan has been granted.

subfiles.title: Embassy letter facilitating del Castillo's passage
subfiles.from: Max V. Krebs, American Embassy, Montevideo
subfiles.to: Francisco José del Castillo y Campos
subfiles.about: Quotes the Army clearance cable for use in securing transportation to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy gives del Castillo written evidence that SCAP approved his entry as chief of the Spanish diplomatic mission.

subfiles.title: Department letter transmitting Esat Mahmut Karakurt's application
subfiles.from: Walter J. Marx, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: George H. Hendricks, Pacific Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP consideration and a permit for Turkish national Esat Mahmut Karakurt.
subfiles.summary: The Department forwards Karakurt's application and notes that he is currently in San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Diplomatic note approving Karakurt's visit
subfiles.to: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim of Turkey
subfiles.about: Transmits Karakurt's permit for a seven-day stay in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department reports approval for entry between September 12 and October 12 and asks the Embassy to deliver the permit.

subfiles.title: Commerce memorandum listing approved Japan travelers
subfiles.from: Far Eastern Branch, Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Lists Paul E. Sernau, Andre N. Sbath, and William J. Melson as Commerce-approved applicants.
subfiles.summary: Commerce forwards applications approved subject to final SCAP action.

subfiles.title: Follow-up telegram concerning Nina Chirskoff's travel document
subfiles.about: Asks whether Chirskoff contacted the Consulate and suggests arranging an alternative identity document.
subfiles.summary: The Department seeks prompt action to ensure Chirskoff has an acceptable travel or identity document.

subfiles.title: International Missionary Council mailing envelope
subfiles.to: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Envelope addressed to the Division of Protective Services.
subfiles.summary: Mailing envelope for International Missionary Council correspondence.

subfiles.title: Decker acknowledgment of Möller's military permit
subfiles.from: John W. Decker, International Missionary Council
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Permit No. 3089 and promises to forward it to Möller.
subfiles.summary: Decker thanks the Department for promptly securing Möller's permit and notes that Möller is traveling to San Francisco.

subfiles.title: File charge sheet
subfiles.about: Records internal circulation of the file.
subfiles.summary: Records charge sheet bearing file number 894.111.

subfiles.title: Action slip for Parviz Rustam Kermani
subfiles.from: George H. Hendricks, Pacific Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Clears Kermani to enter Japan for sixty days.
subfiles.summary: Kermani may enter between September 21 and October 21 and must carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Record-copy designation for Tientsin telegram
subfiles.about: Designates an attached Tientsin telegram copy as the record copy.
subfiles.summary: Record-copy form replacing an unreturned original action copy.

subfiles.title: Incoming telegram header sheet
subfiles.about: Header sheet for an incoming telegram whose message text is absent or illegible.
subfiles.summary: Incoming-telegram header stamped September 26, 1949.

subfiles.title: Telegram explaining Japan application procedures to Tientsin
subfiles.about: Explains direct CINCFE application procedures for U.S. citizens and alien employees of American firms.
subfiles.summary: The Department restates April 1949 rules permitting overseas applicants to seek Japan or Okinawa entry through U.S. diplomatic and consular posts directly from CINCFE.

subfiles.title: Central Records filing annotation
subfiles.about: Asks whether the preceding telegram should be filed under 891.111.
subfiles.summary: Brief filing query concerning the appropriate decimal-file classification.

subfiles.title: Action slip for Anthony and Vera Yaholkovsky
subfiles.from: George H. Hendricks, Pacific Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Grants in-transit clearance through Japan while the couple arranges transportation to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Army authorities confirm transit clearance and state that the American Consul at Dairen has been notified.

subfiles.title: Venezuelan Embassy acknowledgment concerning Seijiro Yazawa
subfiles.from: José Rafael Pocaterra, Embassy of Venezuela
subfiles.about: Acknowledges information about Yazawa's proposed journey from Japan to Venezuela.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy reports that it has forwarded the Department's information concerning Seijiro Yazawa to the Venezuelan Government.

subfiles.title: V. Walter Shriro application for permission to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests permission for Shriro to conduct business-policy discussions in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Shriro Trading Corporation seeks entry for Canadian representative V. Walter Shriro to discuss company policy in Tokyo. The application cites substantial prewar textile business and a former connection with the firm's Shanghai affiliate.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing Shriro's Military Permit No. 5176
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Transmits an indefinite-stay entry permit valid from October 6, 1949, to April 6, 1950.
subfiles.summary: The Department sends Shriro his Army permit and advises that no U.S. exit permit is required.

subfiles.title: Commerce memorandum on Hargrove and Shriro
subfiles.from: Far Eastern Branch, Department of Commerce
subfiles.to: Leonelda Mellor, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Forwards Commerce-approved applications for Donald Hargrove and V. Walter Shriro.
subfiles.summary: Commerce recommends the two applicants subject to final SCAP approval.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 863 concerning Wilhelm Bathge
subfiles.about: Submits Bathge's application to visit Japan as a private commercial entrant.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy describes German textile engineer Wilhelm Bathge's plan to negotiate purchases of Japanese automatic looms and machinery. Bathge expected to travel from Germany to Tokyo for about six weeks and held a Brazilian travel document valid until August 1951.

subfiles.title: Airgram redirecting Bathge's application to the Brazilian mission in Tokyo
subfiles.about: Advises that Bathge must apply through the newly established Brazilian mission in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The Department redirects the case under the revised diplomatic-channel procedure.

subfiles.title: Charge slip for Bathge correspondence
subfiles.about: Records charging of the Bathge despatch and reply airgram.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip for Despatch 863 and Airgram A-464.

subfiles.title: Peiping telegram concerning Chuang Pao-ching's proposed Japan visit
subfiles.about: Requests guidance on allowing a Hong Kong trader already engaged with Japan to make a business visit.
subfiles.summary: Clubb describes Chuang Pao-ching's shipping and commodity interests, the Hua Feng Company's assistance to returning Japanese nationals, and a possible voyage aboard a chartered Italian ship. He asks whether Chuang may proceed alone or with Chin Ting-chih.

subfiles.title: Interim reply to Peiping on the Chuang case
subfiles.about: Reports that Peiping's telegram has been forwarded to SCAP for decision.
subfiles.summary: The Department promises to advise Peiping as soon as SCAP responds.

subfiles.title: Telegram forwarding the Chuang case to SCAP
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards Peiping's inquiry and requests SCAP's decision.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks SCAP to rule on the proposed Japan travel of Chuang Pao-ching.

subfiles.title: File charge-out card
subfiles.about: Later administrative card recording an item charged from the file.
subfiles.summary: Charge-out card stamped July 13, 1955.

subfiles.title: Airgram requesting a decision on Hans Friedel's return to Japan
subfiles.about: Requests advice on whether former Japan resident Hans Friedel may reenter the country.
subfiles.summary: The Department recounts Friedel's prewar residence, marriage to a Japanese national, claimed anti-Nazi record, and forced 1947 repatriation. German occupation authorities found no objection to an exit permit if Japan authorized his entry.

subfiles.title: Operations memorandum requesting a Colombian visa for George Sauerland
subfiles.to: Yokohama Branch, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Requests issuance of a Colombian visa to German national George Sauerland.
subfiles.summary: Yokohama is asked to issue the visa if no information makes Sauerland's entry into the Western Hemisphere undesirable.

subfiles.title: Informal translation of Colombian Embassy Note No. 1744
subfiles.about: Requests American assistance in obtaining a Colombian visa for George Sauerland.
subfiles.summary: Colombia seeks help enabling Sauerland to leave Japan for contracted employment in Colombia.

subfiles.title: Colombian Embassy Note No. 1744 in Spanish
subfiles.about: Spanish original requesting visa assistance for George Sauerland.
subfiles.summary: Original Spanish text of Colombia's request on Sauerland's behalf.

subfiles.title: Department acknowledgment of the Sauerland request
subfiles.about: Reports that the Sauerland matter has been referred to the Department's Yokohama representative.
subfiles.summary: The Department promises to inform the Colombian Embassy when a reply arrives.

subfiles.title: Commerce memorandum approving Albert Evan Small
subfiles.from: Far Eastern Branch, Department of Commerce
subfiles.to: Leonelda Mellor, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Forwards Small's Commerce-approved travel application for final SCAP action.
subfiles.summary: Commerce recommends Albert Evan Small's proposed Japan visit from October 25 to November 25.

subfiles.title: Albert Evan Small application for permission to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests a thirty-day visit to investigate restoration of prewar file sales in Japan.
subfiles.summary: British representative Albert Evan Small proposes to assess conditions and reestablish Nicholson File Company's prewar dealer relationships. He planned to visit Yokohama, Tokyo, Kobe, Osaka, and Kyoto by ship around late October or November.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing Small's military permit
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Transmits Small's Army permit for entry and an indefinite stay.
subfiles.summary: The Department encloses the military permit and notes the blanket waiver of U.S. exit permits.

subfiles.title: Telegram authorizing Donald Nimmo Hargrove's entry
subfiles.about: Communicates permission for Hargrove to enter Japan for sixty days.
subfiles.summary: The Consul is instructed to give Hargrove a certified copy of the clearance telegram and ensure he carries passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Military clearance memorandum for Donald Nimmo Hargrove
subfiles.from: George H. Hendricks, Pacific Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Records Hargrove's sixty-day entry clearance and asks that the appropriate agency be notified.
subfiles.summary: Hargrove is cleared to enter Japan between October 15 and November 15, 1949.

subfiles.title: Donald Nimmo Hargrove application for permission to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests entry for Hargrove to help rehabilitate the company's Japanese subsidiary.
subfiles.summary: The company describes Hargrove as a British specialist needed to restore assembly and business operations in Japan. It cites its seventy-percent ownership of the subsidiary, extensive prewar sales, and a planned six-month stay beginning in mid-October.

subfiles.title: Commerce memorandum forwarding Hargrove and Shriro applications
subfiles.from: Milton A. Berger, Department of Commerce
subfiles.to: Leonelda Mellor, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Lists Hargrove and Shriro as Commerce-approved applicants subject to SCAP approval.
subfiles.summary: Commerce forwards the two commercial-travel applications and their desired entry arrangements.

subfiles.title: Circular airgram on applications for permission to enter Japan
subfiles.about: Explains which diplomatic missions or protecting powers must submit foreign nationals' Japan-entry applications.
subfiles.summary: The airgram lists countries maintaining missions in Tokyo and countries represented by protecting powers. Nationals of other countries may apply through their governments to the Department, while existing rules remain for alien employees of American firms. Recipient posts are instructed to notify subordinate Foreign Service establishments.

subfiles.title: Department reply concerning Carlos Hounie Fleurquin
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP's response concerning Fleurquin's proposed return to his diplomatic post.
subfiles.summary: SCAP had received no entry request or evidence of Fleurquin's return but still regarded him as accredited because Uruguay had not notified otherwise.

subfiles.title: Internal note on the Fleurquin inquiry
subfiles.from: Leonelda Mellor, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records that the Pacific Military Permit Branch would transmit Uruguay's information to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Mellor notes consultation with Mrs. Flickinger and pending SCAP advice.

subfiles.title: Informal translation of Uruguay's note concerning Fleurquin
subfiles.about: Requests notification to SCAP that Fleurquin intends to resume his duties in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Uruguay asks the Department to facilitate the return of its diplomatic agent, whose functions SCAP recognized in February 1948.

subfiles.title: Uruguayan Embassy Note No. 758/949 in Spanish
subfiles.about: Spanish original announcing Fleurquin's intended return to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Original Spanish version of Uruguay's request concerning its diplomatic agent.

subfiles.title: SCAP telegram denying José Ferrer's entry request
subfiles.about: Reports that Ferrer's proposed entry cannot be approved under existing clearance standards.
subfiles.summary: SCAP limits entry to approved official business or short transit with an onward destination and therefore denies Ferrer's request.

subfiles.title: Shriro acknowledgment of military permit
subfiles.from: V. Walter Shriro, Shriro Trading Corporation
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the permit and thanks the Department for prompt handling.
subfiles.summary: Shriro confirms that the entry permit arrived.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding a Japan travel application to Ann Kallmer
subfiles.from: John M. Allison, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs
subfiles.about: Responds to Kallmer's request for assistance by enclosing an entry application form.
subfiles.summary: Allison explains that the appropriate Department division will notify Kallmer after considering her completed application.

subfiles.title: Peiping telegram on Hua Feng trade negotiations
subfiles.about: Reports negotiations involving Hong Kong cotton, Manchurian soybeans, shipping, and loosened regional trade controls.
subfiles.summary: Chin Ting-chih reports proposed cotton-for-soybean barter, coordinated Hong Kong suppliers, possible use of Jardine vessels, and guaranteed loading at Yingkou. Clubb also describes eased salt-export and interregional trade restrictions caused by severe economic pressures.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 712 on Soviet entries and departures
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Explains the dispute over applying customs, immigration, and quarantine controls to Soviet personnel.
subfiles.summary: SCAP ended an interim procedure that had allowed composite Soviet property declarations after discovering abuses. A September 24 Soviet flight was cancelled when personnel and crew refused baggage inspection, prompting exchanged protests. Sebald supports equal application of the regulations while recommending courtesy and leniency to avoid unnecessary friction.

subfiles.title: Letter requiring Soviet compliance with entry and exit regulations
subfiles.from: John H. Chiles for the Chief of Staff, SCAP
subfiles.about: Clarifies that Soviet personnel are subject to current customs, immigration, and quarantine regulations.
subfiles.summary: Chiles cites the applicable SCAP circulars and states that future Soviet entry or exit applications must affirm understanding of and compliance with them.

subfiles.title: Derevyanko protest over inspection of Soviet personnel
subfiles.about: Protests attempted inspections and military-police escorting of Soviet personnel at Haneda.
subfiles.summary: Derevyanko contends that American customs officials unlawfully prevented the departure of Soviet diplomatic couriers, staff, and an aircraft crew by demanding baggage inspections. He insists that the former exemption continue and that augmented military-police escorts cease.

subfiles.title: Almond reply affirming SCAP inspection authority
subfiles.from: Edward M. Almond for the Supreme Commander
subfiles.about: Rejects the Soviet protest and insists on compliance with uniform customs and clearance requirements.
subfiles.summary: Almond states that SCAP's authority over occupation controls is exclusive and that routine inspections apply to Soviet staff like other nondiplomatic personnel. He also cites S. Y. Fomichev's failure to submit required technical reports as a separate obstacle to departure clearance.
